reason: Conversation 1 correctly framed pulsing as airflow protection, kept the homeowner to safe user-level checks (bin, airways, cold-water filter wash with full drying), and reached the right no-part conclusion in three turns without ever pushing a battery or filter purchase. Conversation 2 got to the same fix but repeatedly steered toward 'likely the battery' and replacement parts (filter at £10-15, new battery), contradicted itself on the V8 filter layout, and pushed a non-Dyson 'run it with no filter' test that it admitted lets dust reach the motor, which is an unsupported and mildly risky step for a problem that was just a clogged filter and wand blockage. Conversation 1's only wart is a reflexive 'switch off and unplug' line at the end of a solved case, which is trivial next to Conversation 2's unsupported battery lean and part nudging.
